thread:
olivia: FYI prod-eu proxies started failing mTLS handshakes ~2m ago, seeing a bunch of KMS decrypt DENY in audit logs :grimacing:
vikram: logs? service? link?
olivia: proxy-ingress-eu, errors show `kms:Decrypt` denied for service-account `svc-proxy@redwood-eu` — looks like an RBAC tweak went out in the last deploy window.  https://log.example.com/entries/abc123
sec-eng-jordan: can you paste the audit lines (redact tokens)? curious: is this deny coming from KMS IAM or from our keystore agent?
olivia: pasted snippet:
```
timestamp=2026-03-21T10:02:14Z level=warn proxy=proxy-ingress-eu principal=svc-proxy@redwood-eu action=kms:Decrypt result=Denied reason="iam:Denied" key=projects/…/locations/europe-west2/keyR
```
lina: that looks like the IAM binding for the KMS key lost the `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` for that SA. we pushed an rbac patch to `infra-iam` ~10:00Z.
vikram: rollback plan? can we reapply old binding quickly?
sec-eng-jordan: yes — two options: 1) reapply the previous IAM binding (fast), 2) grant a temporary allow via a grants-overlay while we debug. pref to reapply exact previous binding to minimize blast radius.
sre-ryan: impact: ~20% of EU traffic is falling back to warm-cache and some downstream timeouts. filing pager note.
ops-mike: reapplying the old binding now — running `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding keyR --member=serviceAccount:svc-proxy@redwood-eu --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`
rotator-bot: detected cert rotator job for eu proxy at 09:58Z with status=SUCCESS. rotator config shows `use_kms:true` and key_id:keyR.
lina: hmm rotator succeeded but SA lost permission right after. suspect infra-iam PR had an unintended removal. tagging @infra-team for rollback audit.
vikram: while Mike reapplies, can we patch proxy to fallback to locally cached key material for 5m? quick config toggle: `ROTATOR_FALLBACK=true` in deploy config.
ops-mike: applied IAM binding at 10:05:21Z; KMS `Decrypt` calls are now returning 200 in logs. rolling restart of proxy pods to pick up state. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/proxy-ingress-eu`
olivia: handshakes slowly recovering, error rate down from 18% -> 2% over 4 mins :tada:
sec-eng-jordan: good. next steps: 1) identify infra-iam PR that removed binding; 2) create a preflight test that validates KMS decrypt with our service accounts during deploy; 3) add an alert for `iam:Denied` on KMS key to catch immediately.
lina: adding a regression test in rotator CI to call `gcloud kms decrypt` with a test SA; will open a patch.
vikram: I'll own the alert and runbook update (add mitigation steps and contact list).
sre-ryan: capture timeline in incident channel and save logs for postmortem. I'm starting incident doc: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-031
olivia: question — do we also need to review cross-region key policies? could same RBAC gating break failover to us-east?
sec-eng-jordan: yes, recommend we ensure DR SA permissions exist in all region-key bindings (us-east, eu, apac). I'll make a checklist and run a scan.
ops-mike: note: rotator-bot triggered a cert rotation earlier — that sequence exposed the permission gap quickly. we should add a pre-rotation KMS smoke check.
lina: agree. I'll add smoke check to rotator job: `kms.decrypt(test_ciphertext)` and abort rotation if fails.
vikram: vulnerability triage: low likelihood of exploit here but high availability impact. mark severity P2; we prevented customer data exposure.
sec-eng-jordan: we should also audit who can change `infra-iam` bindings; creating short-term MFA + approval gate for KMS changes.
ops-mike: created temporary approval flow in the infra-iam repo (PR: https://git.example/infra-iam/pulls/987) — needs 2 approvers.
olivia: thanks all — ping me if there are residual errors. I'll add this thread to postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
